etymology.story: Cross the basis pontis from side to side.

info.explanation: Pontocerebellar axons crossing the midline of the basis pons to the opposite middle cerebellar peduncle.

facts.function: Convey cortical information to the contralateral cerebellum.

lists.group: Caudal Pons – Level of Facial Colliculus

etymology.story: Hill on the floor of the fourth ventricle created by facial nerve fibres.

info.explanation: Bump on the floor of the fourth ventricle formed by facial nerve axons looping around the abducens nucleus.

facts.function: Landmark of the caudal pons.
facts.passes: Facial motor axons; abducens nucleus lies beneath.
facts.lesion: Lesion affects CN VI and VII: ipsilateral lateral gaze palsy and facial palsy.

lists.group: Caudal Medulla – Level of Cuneate & Gracile Tubercles
In mid-sagittal / longitudinal section of brainstem

etymology.story: Named for the shape on the ventral medulla (Greek pyramis, from Egyptian pyramids).

info.explanation: Paired ventral medullary bulges containing the corticospinal tracts.

facts.function: Carry descending motor fibres (UMN) to the spinal cord.
facts.lesion: Medial medullary syndrome: contralateral hemiparesis.
facts.connections: ~90% decussate at the pyramidal decussation.

etymology.story: Named for the olive-shaped bulge lateral to the pyramids.

info.explanation: Bulge on the lateral medulla overlying the inferior olivary nucleus.

facts.function: Landmark for inferior olivary nucleus, relay to cerebellum.
facts.lesion: Hypertrophic olivary degeneration; palatal myoclonus.

etymology.story: Tuberculum is a diminutive of tuber, "swelling" and cuneus "wedge".

info.explanation: Bulge on the dorsal medulla overlying the nucleus cuneatus.

facts.function: Landmark for the nucleus cuneatus (upper-body DCML relay).
facts.connections: Overlies nucleus cuneatus.

etymology.story: Gracilis means slender.

info.explanation: Bulge on the dorsal medulla overlying the nucleus gracilis.

facts.function: Landmark for the nucleus gracilis (lower-body DCML relay).
facts.connections: Overlies nucleus gracilis.

etymology.story: Latin for "barrier" or "bolt", from obicere "to throw against"; the obex is the caudal angle of the fourth ventricle floor, where the ventricle closes into the central canal.

info.explanation: Caudal apex of the fourth ventricle where it narrows to the central canal.

facts.function: Landmark for the junction of medulla and spinal cord.

etymology.story: Postrema is the superlative of posterus: the most posterior area, at the caudal end of the floor of the fourth ventricle.

info.explanation: Circumventricular organ at the caudal floor of the fourth ventricle lacking a blood-brain barrier.

facts.function: Chemoreceptor trigger zone: detects toxins and triggers vomiting.
facts.lesion: Lesion causes intractable hiccups and vomiting in neuromyelitis optica.
facts.connections: Projects to the solitary nucleus and parabrachial nucleus.

etymology.story: Cisterna is a Roman underground water tank, from cista "chest, box"; a cistern is an enlarged pocket of subarachnoid space filled with CSF.

info.explanation: Subarachnoid cistern around the interpeduncular fossa containing the basilar tip and its branches.

facts.function: CSF-filled space around the circle of Willis arteries.
facts.passes: CN III runs through it; posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries.
facts.supply: Basilar tip and posterior communicating arteries.
facts.lesion: Subarachnoid haemorrhage blood collects here.

lists.group: Rostral Midbrain – Level of Superior Colliculus
Caudal Midbrain – Level of Inferior Colliculus

etymology.story: A grey-matter ring around the cerebral aqueduct.

info.explanation: Grey matter surrounding the cerebral aqueduct of the midbrain.

facts.function: Descending modulation of pain, defensive behaviours, autonomic and vocalisation responses.
facts.lesion: Stimulation produces analgesia; lesions disrupt consciousness.
facts.connections: Receives from hypothalamus and amygdala; projects to the raphe nuclei.

lists.group: Rostral Midbrain – Level of Superior Colliculus

etymology.story: Appears pinkish-red in fresh tissue because of its rich blood supply and iron-containing pigments.

info.explanation: Round midbrain nucleus at the level of the superior colliculus, in the tegmentum.

facts.function: Origin of the rubrospinal tract that facilitates flexor tone of the contralateral upper limb.
facts.passes: Receives dentate fibres via the superior cerebellar peduncle after they decussate.
facts.supply: Posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries (paramedian branches).
facts.lesion: Claude syndrome and Benedikt syndrome: oculomotor palsy with contralateral ataxia and tremor.
facts.connections: Dentate (contralateral) -> red nucleus -> rubrospinal tract (crosses again).

lists.group: Rostral Midbrain – Level of Superior Colliculus

etymology.story: Oculomotor means "eye mover".

info.explanation: Somatic motor nucleus at the level of the superior colliculus ventral to the cerebral aqueduct.

facts.function: Provides motor fibres to four extraocular muscles and levator palpebrae.
facts.supply: Basilar tip and posterior cerebral artery paramedian branches.
facts.lesion: Ptosis, down-and-out eye, dilated pupil (CN III palsy).
facts.connections: Superior rectus subnucleus is contralateral; others ipsilateral.

lists.group: Rostral Midbrain – Level of Superior Colliculus

etymology.story: An eponym for the two men who each described this small cell group beside the oculomotor nucleus in the 1880s. The Latin name, nucleus accessorius nervi oculomotorii, calls it the accessory nucleus of the oculomotor nerve.

info.explanation: Parasympathetic nucleus dorsal to the main oculomotor nucleus.

facts.function: Pupillary constriction and accommodation via the ciliary ganglion.
facts.passes: Preganglionic parasympathetic fibres travel with CN III to the ciliary ganglion.
facts.lesion: Loss gives a fixed dilated pupil (blown pupil in uncal herniation).

lists.group: Rostral Midbrain – Level of Superior Colliculus
Caudal Midbrain – Level of Inferior Colliculus

etymology.story: The nucleus appears dark in unstained tissue because of neuromelanin in dopaminergic neurons.

info.explanation: Midbrain nucleus dorsal to the cerebral peduncles with a pars compacta (dopamine) and a pars reticulata (GABA output).

facts.function: Dopaminergic input to the striatum and motor output of the basal ganglia.
facts.supply: Posterior cerebral and posterior communicating arteries.
facts.lesion: Loss of dopaminergic neurons gives Parkinson disease (bradykinesia, rigidity, resting tremor).
facts.connections: Nigrostriatal pathway to caudate and putamen.

lists.group: Rostral Midbrain – Level of Superior Colliculus
Cranial nerves I-VIII, IX/X, and XII on a wet specimen
Cranial nerves I-XII on an image or schematic

etymology.story: CN III, the nerve that moves the eye.

info.explanation: Cranial nerve III emerging from the interpeduncular fossa; carries somatic motor to four extraocular muscles and levator palpebrae and parasympathetic fibres.

facts.function: Moves the eye (up, down, in), raises the eyelid, constricts the pupil and accommodates the lens.
facts.passes: Superior orbital fissure into the orbit.
facts.lesion: Compression (posterior communicating aneurysm, uncal herniation) gives a blown pupil first because parasympathetic fibres run on the outside; diabetic infarcts spare the pupil.
facts.connections: Nucleus at the level of the superior colliculus.
